epitaph: The PWF Challenge Title's own dated ledger runs three reigns deep and closes mid-chain: Crusader Chrome won the title's own first-ever match — a fatal four-way over Theros Macalvia, The Fro, and Maxwell Powers — at Saturday Night Havoc, 24 March 2001; Power G won it from him on 7 April; Rye Hazwaki won it from Power G on 18 April, the ledger's own last entry.
name: PWF Challenge Title
notes: The fed's own four remaining named titles (European, Hardcore, Extreme, Tag Team) are named on the Records page but no ledger, reign, or dated mention survives for any of them in this capture. The World and US Titles are also unledgered here, but their own reigns are independently documented from other primary sources — see pwf-powersite-world and pwf-powersite-us.

name: PWF World Title
epitaph: The PWF World Title's own surviving record is a two-reign, seven-month fragment either side of a gap the capture never closes: Jason "The Goat" Doods won it in a Trio Ladder Match at THE PWF REBIRTH, the fed's own 1 October 2000 relaunch, and Crusader Chrome won it from an unnamed prior holder in a Double Jeopardy Ladder Match at War Games, 27 May 2001, with Bloodbath's interference — the assist that formed the OutKasts. No document in this capture records how the title moved between those two nights; by 24 March 2001, Michael Pellington is announcing a fresh tournament to crown a new champion, and Antonio Gambino is publicly demanding the belt back as the fed's own pre-hibernation titleholder "the first time around."
notes: Several wrestlers' own bio cards claim further, undated World Title reigns from the pre-hibernation "old PWF" era (Gambino, Eraser, DeMoN, Blackbird, Firestorm among them) — bio-attested only, with no date surviving to sequence any of them against each other or against this ledger, so none are entered as reign rows. See each character's own tenure note.

name: PWF US Title
epitaph: The PWF US Title's only documented reign in this capture is Rye Hazwaki's, won in the same Double Jeopardy Ladder Match that crowned Crusader Chrome World Champion at War Games, 27 May 2001, with Havok's interference — the same assist that formed the OutKasts.
notes: Several wrestlers' own bio cards claim further, undated US Title reigns from the pre-hibernation "old PWF" era (Crusader Chrome among them) — bio-attested only, not entered as reign rows for the same reason as the World Title above.
